Language of instruction: The course will be given in English

The course aims to give the students a good overview of the most relevant areas in privacy technologies for digital information. The course will provide an introduction to the various types of privacy risks and a range of tools/techniques to address those risks.

Knowledge and understanding
      For a passing grade the student must

Competences and skills
      For a passing grade the student must

Judgement and approach
      For a passing grade the student must

As engineers you will be designing, implementing, or managing electronic systems and services that in most cases have privacy implications. For example, ambient sensors and biomedical implants collect, process, store, and communicate (sometimes highly sensitive) data related to individuals; the data generated by ubiquitous electronic communications provides detailed insight into people’s activities and lifestyle; and the personalization of multimedia applications and services relies on learning about individuals’ most intimate preferences and adapting to them. The goal of the course is to give an introduction to privacy technologies. We will explain the various types of privacy risks and introduce a range of existing privacy technologies that address these risks. Some areas are dealt with in more depth.
Building blocks for privacy: different tools to design privacy preserving applications. Includes private information retrieval, oblivious transfer, anonymous credentials, anonymous tokens etc.
Communication Privacy: VPNs; Anonymous communication systems: Oblivious HTTP, Tor, Mixnets, DC-nets; Censorship and anti-censorship systems.
Data privacy and data anonymization: Importance of data protection, k-anonymity, re-identification attacks, differential privacy, privacy-utility tradeoff.
Web privacy: web tracking techniques, cookies, device fingerprinting, prevention techniques.
The course also includes two projects. The result will be summarized in a technical report and also presented on a seminar.

Grading scale: TH - (U, 3, 4, 5) - (Fail, Three, Four, Five)
Assessment:

To obtain a grade of 3, a pass is required in the projects and presentations ‘Project and Theory’ and ‘Implementation and Experiments’. Higher grades (4 or 5) may be awarded based on optional written reports and/or oral presentations.

The examiner, in consultation with Disability Support Services, may deviate from the regular form of examination in order to provide a permanently disabled student with a form of examination equivalent to that of a student without a disability.

Modules
Code: 0126. Name: Project and Theory. 

Credits: 4.0. Grading scale: TH - (U, 3, 4, 5).
        
          Assessment: A passing grade for the project and a passing group presentation are required. Optional individual reports and/or presentations may be submitted for grades 4 or 5.
        
        
          The module includes: Compulsory project and compulsory presentation
        
        
        
Code: 0226. Name: Implementation and Experimentation. 

Credits: 3.5. Grading scale: TH - (U, 3, 4, 5).
        
          Assessment: A passing grade for the project and a passing group presentation are required. Optional individual reports and/or presentations may be submitted for grades 4 or 5.
        
        
          The module includes: Compulsory project and compulsory presentation

Assumed prior knowledge: 
        Basic knowledge about computer networks and computer security is expected to attend this course, such as in EITA25. 
        
The number of participants is limited to: No
Kursen överlappar följande kurser: 
EITF06
